note: Featured cases for the Third Country / Removal Trace video. Every field is drawn from routes.json, circuits.json, and the two companion blog posts; nothing here is invented. Coordinates are joined at runtime from routes.json.countries by ISO3, so this file carries no lon/lat except usCentroid. usLocation is null for every case because no source publishes the detention site; the loader pins these on usCentroid labeled LOCATION NOT PUBLIC. Alves, Natalia E., and Etoria from the original brief are intentionally absent until their sources are supplied; drop them in as new objects and they render with no code change.

cases.name: Ansumana S. v. Blanche
cases.quote: to any country other than the Ivory Coast that will accept him
cases.quoteSource: 2006 immigration judge removal order, as described in the world-map post
cases.notes: Withholding as to Ivory Coast since a 2006 IJ order; DHS later tried to send him to Sierra Leone. The court barred the removal even though Sierra Leone had given diplomatic assurances, so the white arc stops and shatters with a COURT ORDER tag.

sources.label: Ansumana S. v. Blanche (D. Minn. 2026) — via companion world map

cases.name: Ibarra-Perez v. United States
cases.quote: has been rejected by every other circuit that has considered it
cases.quoteSource: Judge Bea, dissenting from denial of rehearing en banc, on the panel's §1252(g) reading
cases.notes: A Cuban man with withholding as to Cuba was sent to Mexico about 16 hours after notice, over his repeated objection. The Ninth Circuit held §1252(g) did not bar his damages suit. The arc completes to Mexico; notice clock reads 16h.

sources.label: Ibarra-Perez v. United States, 154 F.4th 989 (9th Cir. 2025)
9th Cir. order denying rehearing en banc (June 25, 2026)

cases.name: Lopez v. U.S. ICE
cases.notes: A Bolivian woman with withholding and CAT deferral as to Bolivia, appearing without a lawyer, opposed removal to the Congo. The court lifted the stay, holding the Congo's diplomatic assurances gave her all the process due. The one government win; arc completes. Notice clock 0h (assurances).

sources.label: Lopez v. ICE, 832 F. Supp. 3d 617 (W.D. Tex. 2026)
Companion world map: why a third country

cases.name: D.V.D. v. DHS — the South Sudan flight
cases.notes: Eight men on one flight at the center of the D.V.D. contempt dispute; one was South Sudanese, seven were third country nationals. The repo does not document the Djibouti/Camp Lemonnier layover or a '6 weeks held' figure, so via is null and no HELD label is shown until a source is supplied. Date is approximate (May 2025 flight) and should be confirmed before it is shown on screen.

sources.label: D.V.D. v. DHS, No. 26-426 — South Sudan destination note

cases.name: D.A. v. Noem — Ghana, onward removal
cases.notes: People already flown to Ghana feared onward removal to the home countries U.S. judges had protected them from. The court held it could not order Ghana to keep them. chainReturn is true, but the repo names no specific onward ISO3, so onwardTo is null and the aftermath beat shows a generic SENT ON TO HOME COUNTRY tag rather than a fabricated country arc.

sources.label: D.A. v. Noem (D.D.C. 2025) — TRO denied Sept. 15, 2025
Ghana destination note: sent some onward

cases.name: Cruz-Medina v. Noem
cases.notes: A man with CAT protection as to Honduras; the court barred removal to Mexico until an immigration judge reviews his negative fear finding. Arc toward Mexico shatters with a COURT ORDER tag.

cases.name: E.D.Q.C. v. Warden
cases.notes: A Venezuelan man sent to the CECOT prison in El Salvador. The court rejected §1252 bars and allowed discovery into whether he remained in U.S. custody. This is a jurisdiction case, so no barred-country beat is shown (barred is null).

cases.name: Quiroz Zapata v. Mullin
cases.notes: A Colombian woman was sent to the Congo, which had not agreed to accept her. The court ordered her return. The arc completes to the Congo, then a dashed return arc brings her back (outcome: returned).

cases.name: Habeas petition, No. 2:26-cv-08574
cases.notes: A woman with withholding as to Guinea was arrested for removal to Ghana; the court barred the transfer. Arc toward Ghana shatters with a COURT ORDER tag. No public date for the order in the repo, so date is null.
